question: A new subdivision main connects to an existing trunk main through a tee and a gate valve at the junction. What does that gate valve let an operator do when the new main needs a repair?
correctAnswer: Isolate the new main while the trunk main stays in service
explanation: A valve at the junction lets crews shut off only the branch main, so the trunk main can keep serving its customers during the repair.
options: Raise the pressure in the trunk main during the repair work
Isolate the new main while the trunk main stays in service
Remove air from the trunk main while crews open the new main
Measure the flow in the trunk main while the new main is drained
optionA: Raise the pressure in the trunk main during the repair work
optionB: Isolate the new main while the trunk main stays in service
optionC: Remove air from the trunk main while crews open the new main
optionD: Measure the flow in the trunk main while the new main is drained
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Mains and Services. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: A hydrant barrel in a cold climate system stays dry between uses. Which component drains the barrel after the hydrant is shut following a flow test?
correctAnswer: A drain port at the base that opens when the valve closes
explanation: Dry barrel hydrants drain through ports at the base once the main valve closes, which keeps standing water from freezing in the barrel.
options: A check valve fitted inside the hydrant hose nozzle cap
A pressure relief valve mounted on top of the bonnet
A drain port at the base that opens when the valve closes
A vacuum breaker installed inside the steamer port
optionA: A check valve fitted inside the hydrant hose nozzle cap
optionB: A pressure relief valve mounted on top of the bonnet
optionC: A drain port at the base that opens when the valve closes
optionD: A vacuum breaker installed inside the steamer port

question: A residential service has a corporation stop at the main and a curb stop near the property line. Where is the water meter usually installed on this type of service?
correctAnswer: Inside the building, downstream of the curb stop
explanation: On a typical residential service the meter sits inside the building past the curb stop, where it is protected from freezing and easy to read.
options: Inside the building, downstream of the curb stop
At the main, upstream of the corporation stop valve
In the street, inside the curb stop valve chamber box
At the hydrant, beside the nearest main line valve
optionA: Inside the building, downstream of the curb stop
optionB: At the main, upstream of the corporation stop valve
optionC: In the street, inside the curb stop valve chamber box
optionD: At the hydrant, beside the nearest main line valve
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Meters and Service Connections. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: An operator measures the free chlorine residual at the far end of a pressure zone and finds it lower than at the entry point on the same day. Which factor most directly explains the drop along the way?
correctAnswer: Chlorine is consumed by reactions as the water travels and ages
explanation: Free chlorine reacts with material in the water and on pipe walls as it travels, so the residual falls as water age increases.
options: Chlorine is added by the pipe walls as the water travels and ages
Pressure converts free chlorine into chloramines inside the pipes
Water meters strip free chlorine from the water passing through them
Chlorine is consumed by reactions as the water travels and ages
optionA: Chlorine is added by the pipe walls as the water travels and ages
optionB: Pressure converts free chlorine into chloramines inside the pipes
optionC: Water meters strip free chlorine from the water passing through them
optionD: Chlorine is consumed by reactions as the water travels and ages
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Chlorine Residual Maintenance. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: During unidirectional flushing, crews open one hydrant and close selected valves before moving on to the next segment. What does closing those valves accomplish in the segment being flushed?
correctAnswer: It forces flow through the segment in one direction at higher speed
explanation: Closing valves sets a single flow path, so water moves one way through the segment fast enough to scour deposits from the pipe wall.
options: It lets flushed water recirculate until it runs clear at the hydrant
It forces flow through the segment in one direction at higher speed
It raises the static pressure in every street adjoining the segment
It allows two hydrants to drain the same segment from both ends
optionA: It lets flushed water recirculate until it runs clear at the hydrant
optionB: It forces flow through the segment in one direction at higher speed
optionC: It raises the static pressure in every street adjoining the segment
optionD: It allows two hydrants to drain the same segment from both ends
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Flushing Programs. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: An elevated tank fills overnight and drains during the morning peak. Which system condition most directly causes the tank to start draining in the morning?
correctAnswer: Demand in the zone rises above the supply entering it, so the level falls
explanation: An elevated tank drains by gravity whenever zone demand exceeds the inflow, and it refills when inflow exceeds demand.
options: Demand in the zone rises above the supply entering it, so the level falls
The tank outlet valve is opened by hand each morning by the operator
Overnight pumping reverses and pulls water back out of the tank
Air pressure above the stored water pushes the level down at sunrise
optionA: Demand in the zone rises above the supply entering it, so the level falls
optionB: The tank outlet valve is opened by hand each morning by the operator
optionC: Overnight pumping reverses and pulls water back out of the tank
optionD: Air pressure above the stored water pushes the level down at sunrise
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Elevated Storage. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: Two taps are fed from the same elevated tank, and one tap sits 10 m higher than the other with no flow in the connecting main. How does static pressure at the higher tap compare with pressure at the lower tap?
correctAnswer: It is lower, because less head remains above the higher tap
explanation: Static pressure depends on the height of water above the point, so the higher tap has less head above it and lower pressure.
options: It is higher, because the higher tap is closer to the tank
It is the same, because both taps share one pressure zone
It is lower, because less head remains above the higher tap
It is double, because elevation adds pressure as height rises
optionA: It is higher, because the higher tap is closer to the tank
optionB: It is the same, because both taps share one pressure zone
optionC: It is lower, because less head remains above the higher tap
optionD: It is double, because elevation adds pressure as height rises
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Pressure and Head. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: A routine bacteriological sample is collected from a dedicated sampling tap in a neighbourhood. Which step protects the sample from contamination at the tap itself?
correctAnswer: Flush the tap first, then disinfect the outlet before collecting
explanation: Flushing clears stagnant water from the tap and disinfecting the outlet keeps surface contamination out of the sterile bottle.
options: Collect the first water that comes out of the tap opening
Rinse the sterile bottle three times with the sample water
Warm the sample bottle in sunlight before filling it at the tap
Flush the tap first, then disinfect the outlet before collecting
optionA: Collect the first water that comes out of the tap opening
optionB: Rinse the sterile bottle three times with the sample water
optionC: Warm the sample bottle in sunlight before filling it at the tap
optionD: Flush the tap first, then disinfect the outlet before collecting

question: A homeowner reports no water on a January morning while neighbours on the same main have normal supply, and the service line runs shallow beneath the driveway. Which check should the operator make first?
correctAnswer: Check whether the service line has frozen between the main and the house
explanation: Neighbours with normal supply rule out a system outage, and a shallow service in deep cold points first to a frozen service line.
options: Check whether the service line has frozen between the main and the house
Check whether the elevated tank serving the zone has emptied overnight
Check whether a trunk main break has drained the whole pressure zone
Check whether the booster pumps for the zone have tripped offline
optionA: Check whether the service line has frozen between the main and the house
optionB: Check whether the elevated tank serving the zone has emptied overnight
optionC: Check whether a trunk main break has drained the whole pressure zone
optionD: Check whether the booster pumps for the zone have tripped offline

question: Crews must repair a main, and the first isolation valve will not fully close because it has not been operated in years. Which action best limits the shutdown while the work proceeds?
correctAnswer: Close the next valves outward and notify the added affected customers
explanation: Moving the isolation points outward is the controlled way to stop the flow, and the wider shutdown area must be communicated to customers.
options: Force the stuck valve shut with an extended wrench beyond its rated torque
Close the next valves outward and notify the added affected customers
Start the repair with the main still partly live and rely on trench pumps
Open hydrants across the zone to drain water away from the work area
optionA: Force the stuck valve shut with an extended wrench beyond its rated torque
optionB: Close the next valves outward and notify the added affected customers
optionC: Start the repair with the main still partly live and rely on trench pumps
optionD: Open hydrants across the zone to drain water away from the work area
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Valves and Hydrants. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: A commercial account shows a sudden drop in recorded use while the business reports normal operations and no plumbing changes. Which field check best tests whether the meter is under-registering?
correctAnswer: Run a known volume through the meter and compare it with the register
explanation: Passing a measured volume through the meter and comparing it with what the register records directly tests meter accuracy.
options: Read the meter twice on the same day and compare the two readings
Check the static pressure at the curb stop with the building closed
Inspect the corporation stop at the main for a partial obstruction
Run a known volume through the meter and compare it with the register
optionA: Read the meter twice on the same day and compare the two readings
optionB: Check the static pressure at the curb stop with the building closed
optionC: Inspect the corporation stop at the main for a partial obstruction
optionD: Run a known volume through the meter and compare it with the register
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Meters and Service Connections. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: Residuals on a dead end street keep falling between weekly checks while the entry point residual stays steady. Which operator action most directly addresses the cause at that location?
correctAnswer: Flush the dead end to bring in fresher water with a higher residual
explanation: Dead ends hold old water that has lost its residual, and flushing replaces it with fresher water from the active main.
options: Lower the chlorine dose at the entry point to match the dead end
Reduce sampling on the street to once each season instead of weekly
Flush the dead end to bring in fresher water with a higher residual
Close the dead end feed valve so the stale water stays isolated
optionA: Lower the chlorine dose at the entry point to match the dead end
optionB: Reduce sampling on the street to once each season instead of weekly
optionC: Flush the dead end to bring in fresher water with a higher residual
optionD: Close the dead end feed valve so the stale water stays isolated

question: A flushing crew opens a hydrant fully all at once, and a nearby joint begins to leak as pressures swing in the main. Which change prevents that problem on the next segment?
correctAnswer: Open and close the hydrant slowly to avoid pressure transients
explanation: Rapid valve or hydrant movement creates pressure transients that stress joints, so hydrants are opened and closed slowly.
options: Open and close the hydrant slowly to avoid pressure transients
Open the hydrant faster so the pressure wave passes more quickly
Close all customer curb stops on the street before flushing begins
Flush only at night so the pressure swings go unnoticed by customers
optionA: Open and close the hydrant slowly to avoid pressure transients
optionB: Open the hydrant faster so the pressure wave passes more quickly
optionC: Close all customer curb stops on the street before flushing begins
optionD: Flush only at night so the pressure swings go unnoticed by customers

question: A tank level keeps dropping during the day even though zone demand is normal, and the altitude valve at the tank was serviced last week. Which check should the operator make first at the tank?
correctAnswer: Confirm the altitude valve opens to refill the tank at its set level
explanation: The altitude valve controls filling and was just disturbed by service work, so verifying that it opens at its set level comes first.
options: Confirm the tank overflow pipe has not been blocked by nesting birds
Confirm the tank access ladder and hatch are locked and in good repair
Confirm the altitude valve opens to refill the tank at its set level
Confirm the tank exterior coating has not begun to peel near the roof
optionA: Confirm the tank overflow pipe has not been blocked by nesting birds
optionB: Confirm the tank access ladder and hatch are locked and in good repair
optionC: Confirm the altitude valve opens to refill the tank at its set level
optionD: Confirm the tank exterior coating has not begun to peel near the roof

question: A gauge at a pump station reads 420 kPa while a second gauge 20 m higher in the same zone reads much lower with the pumps off and no flow. What explains the lower reading at the higher gauge?
correctAnswer: Elevation head between the gauges reduces pressure at the higher one
explanation: With no flow there is no friction loss, and the pressure difference between the two points is set by the elevation difference between them.
options: Friction in the main removes pressure even when no water is moving
Elevation head between the gauges reduces pressure at the higher one
The higher gauge is farther from the tank, so its pressure decays
Air trapped at the pump station inflates the lower gauge reading
optionA: Friction in the main removes pressure even when no water is moving
optionB: Elevation head between the gauges reduces pressure at the higher one
optionC: The higher gauge is farther from the tank, so its pressure decays
optionD: Air trapped at the pump station inflates the lower gauge reading
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Pressure and Head. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: A routine sample returns a positive total coliform result from a site near a main repair completed two days earlier. Which immediate field action should the operator take?
correctAnswer: Collect repeat samples at the site and at nearby upstream and downstream sites
explanation: A positive result triggers repeat sampling at the original site and at nearby sites on both sides, following the provincial sampling protocol.
options: Advise every customer in the zone to boil water until further notice
Raise the chlorine dose across the whole system before resampling
Wait one week and then collect a single sample at the same site
Collect repeat samples at the site and at nearby upstream and downstream sites
optionA: Advise every customer in the zone to boil water until further notice
optionB: Raise the chlorine dose across the whole system before resampling
optionC: Wait one week and then collect a single sample at the same site
optionD: Collect repeat samples at the site and at nearby upstream and downstream sites

question: A crew taps a live main for a new service using a tapping machine and a tapping valve. What does the tapping valve allow once the cut is made and the machine is removed?
correctAnswer: Control of the new service flow without shutting down the main
explanation: The tapping valve stays on the main after the machine comes off, giving a shutoff point for the new service while the main stays live.
options: Removal of the coupon cut from the main wall after the tap
Testing of the main for leaks at twice its working pressure
Control of the new service flow without shutting down the main
Connection of two trunk mains at different operating pressures
optionA: Removal of the coupon cut from the main wall after the tap
optionB: Testing of the main for leaks at twice its working pressure
optionC: Control of the new service flow without shutting down the main
optionD: Connection of two trunk mains at different operating pressures

question: An air release valve at a high point in a main is found leaking and is then left until it fails in the closed position. Which consequence follows during normal operation?
correctAnswer: Trapped air collects at the high point and restricts the flow capacity
explanation: Air that cannot escape gathers at high points, shrinking the waterway and adding head loss through that section of main.
options: Trapped air collects at the high point and restricts the flow capacity
Chlorine residual at the high point rises as the air pocket grows
The main at the high point drains completely back to the pump hall
Pressure at the high point climbs steadily until a joint separates
optionA: Trapped air collects at the high point and restricts the flow capacity
optionB: Chlorine residual at the high point rises as the air pocket grows
optionC: The main at the high point drains completely back to the pump hall
optionD: Pressure at the high point climbs steadily until a joint separates

question: A commercial property adds an irrigation system with a chemical feed unit, and a new service connection is installed. Which device at the service connection protects the distribution main if system pressure drops suddenly?
correctAnswer: A backflow preventer installed at the service connection point

A backflow preventer installed at the service connection point
A second water meter installed in series at the property line
A check valve on the hydrant lateral nearest the property

question: Hot weather arrives and residuals across the system fall faster than they did in spring at the same entry dose. Which adjustment keeps residuals within the operating target at the far points of the system?
correctAnswer: Increase the chlorine dose leaving the plant to offset the higher demand
explanation: Warm water increases chlorine demand and decay, so the applied dose has to rise to hold the target residual at distant points.
options: Decrease the chlorine dose leaving the plant to match spring conditions
Suspend residual sampling at far points until cooler weather returns
Reduce flushing so less treated water leaves the distribution system

question: A subdivision built in phases has several dead end mains that await future extension loops. Which flushing approach best protects water quality at those dead ends in the meantime?
correctAnswer: Flush each dead end on a planned cycle guided by residual checks there
explanation: Dead ends age water continuously, so they need scheduled flushing with the frequency set by what residual monitoring shows.
options: Flush each dead end on a planned cycle guided by residual checks there
Flush each dead end once at construction and then leave it alone
Flush a dead end only after a customer reports a taste complaint
Flush the looped streets twice as often to cover the dead ends

question: An elevated tank overflows on two straight nights, and a float switch that controls the source pumps is found stuck in the run position. Which repair restores normal level control at the tank?
correctAnswer: Repair or replace the stuck float switch so the pumps stop at high level
explanation: The float switch is the level control that stops the pumps, and a switch stuck on run fills the tank past its high level to the overflow.
options: Raise the tank overflow pipe so the extra water stays in the tank
Throttle the tank inlet valve so the tank fills more slowly at night
Repair or replace the stuck float switch so the pumps stop at high level
Lock the source pumps on manual control until the next inspection
optionA: Raise the tank overflow pipe so the extra water stays in the tank

question: A pressure reducing valve station feeds a low lying zone from a higher zone, and the outlet pressure creeps upward overnight when demand is near zero. Which part of the station should be checked first?
correctAnswer: The pilot control and the seat of the pressure reducing valve
explanation: Rising outlet pressure at no flow points to the reducing valve itself, where a worn seat or a faulty pilot lets high side pressure pass.
options: The check valve on the hydrant lateral across the street
The pilot control and the seat of the pressure reducing valve
The float switch inside the elevated tank in the high zone
The register on the largest meter in the low lying zone

question: Samples from a garden hose bib at one house keep showing poor results while nearby dedicated sampling sites stay clear. Which change gives a sample that represents the water in the main?
correctAnswer: Collect from a dedicated sampling station or a smooth nosed indoor tap

Collect from the hose bib after the hose has been coiled in the sun
Collect from an outdoor tap fitted with a threaded vacuum breaker
Collect from a dedicated sampling station or a smooth nosed indoor tap

question: Pressure on one street drops suddenly and water surfaces at a curb during dry weather. Which first step best confirms whether the source is the main or a service line?
correctAnswer: Close the curb stop and watch whether the surface water flow stops
explanation: If the surfacing water stops when the curb stop closes, the leak is on the service line past that point rather than on the main.

Sound the hydrants on the street and compare their static pressures
Close the curb stop and watch whether the surface water flow stops
Excavate at the wettest point and inspect whatever pipe is found

question: A crew must enter a valve chamber classed as a confined space to repair a leaking packing gland. Which step must the crew complete before anyone enters the chamber?
correctAnswer: Test the atmosphere and set up ventilation with an attendant posted outside
explanation: Confined space entry starts with atmospheric testing, ventilation, and a trained attendant outside before any worker goes in.
options: Test the atmosphere and set up ventilation with an attendant posted outside
Send the fastest worker in alone to finish before gases can build up
Seal the chamber vents so street exhaust stays out during the repair
Have the entrant carry a phone instead of posting an attendant outside

question: A hotel has very low overnight flows and very high morning peak flows, and its single large meter misses most of the overnight use. Which meter arrangement should be selected for this service?
correctAnswer: A compound meter that pairs a large meter with a small bypass meter
explanation: A compound meter registers low flows on its small meter and shifts to the large meter at high flows, covering both ends of the range.
options: A larger single meter sized for the morning peak flow alone
A turbine meter with its strainer removed to cut pressure loss
Two meters in parallel that both register only the peak flows
A compound meter that pairs a large meter with a small bypass meter
optionA: A larger single meter sized for the morning peak flow alone
optionB: A turbine meter with its strainer removed to cut pressure loss

question: A repaired main is returned to service and the residual just downstream falls within hours while the water is slightly cloudy. Which cause and response best fit this pattern?
correctAnswer: Deposits left in the segment exert chlorine demand, so flush the segment and recheck the residual
explanation: Sediment and biofilm disturbed by the repair consume chlorine quickly, and flushing the segment out followed by a residual check is the fitting response.
options: The new pipe adds chlorine to the water, so reduce the entry dose at once
Deposits left in the segment exert chlorine demand, so flush the segment and recheck the residual
Cloudy water protects chlorine from decay, so leave the segment undisturbed
The residual fell because the main is new, so wait a month before checking again

optionB: Deposits left in the segment exert chlorine demand, so flush the segment and recheck the residual

question: Flushing at a hydrant produces clear water, yet customers past the next closed valve still report taste problems and low residuals. Which explanation best fits these results?
correctAnswer: The problem segment lies past that valve and was not actually flushed
explanation: Flushing only cleans the path the water actually travelled, and a closed valve ends that path, leaving the segment beyond it untouched.
options: The flushed segment was cleaned too well and stripped its own lining
The hydrant used for flushing was too close to the elevated tank
The problem segment lies past that valve and was not actually flushed
Clear water at the hydrant proves the whole street was flushed

question: An elevated tank in winter develops surface ice and rising water age because the pumps cycle within a narrow level band near the top. Which operating change improves turnover without risking low zone pressure?
correctAnswer: Widen the pump control level band so more stored water cycles each day
explanation: A wider operating band draws down and refills more of the stored volume daily, which cuts water age while keeping a working reserve.
options: Widen the pump control level band so more stored water cycles each day
Hold the tank level steady at the top so the surface never moves
Drain the tank completely each week and refill it from empty
Stop filling the tank until the ice melts on its own in spring
optionA: Widen the pump control level band so more stored water cycles each day
optionB: Hold the tank level steady at the top so the surface never moves

question: Two pressure zones are separated by a closed boundary valve, and opening it to support a fire flow in the lower zone pulls the higher zone below its pressure target during peak demand. Which long term fix addresses the root problem?
correctAnswer: Add feed capacity, such as a larger main or a booster pump, for the added demand
explanation: The higher zone lacks the capacity to carry the extra load, so the fix is added supply capacity rather than a standing open boundary.
options: Leave the boundary valve open at all times so the zones equalize daily
Raise the lower zone pressure target so it matches the higher zone
Rely on the boundary valve opening for every future peak demand event
Add feed capacity, such as a larger main or a booster pump, for the added demand
optionA: Leave the boundary valve open at all times so the zones equalize daily
optionB: Raise the lower zone pressure target so it matches the higher zone

question: An original sample is positive, the repeat samples at that site are negative, and one repeat sample upstream is positive. Which interpretation and action best fit this set of results?
correctAnswer: Treat the upstream positive as a lead and expand sampling and investigation there
explanation: A negative repeat set at one site does not clear the system when an upstream repeat is positive, so investigation follows the positive result.
options: Declare the system clear because the repeats at the first site were negative
Treat the upstream positive as a lead and expand sampling and investigation there
Resample only the first site monthly and take no other action this season
Assume the laboratory mixed up the bottles and discard all of the results

question: One block of cast iron main has broken three times in two winters while same age mains on adjacent blocks have not broken, and the block sits in wet clay beside a leaking storm sewer. Which decision is best supported by this record?
correctAnswer: Prioritize that block for replacement because local conditions are driving its failures

options: Keep repairing that block and give replacement priority to the oldest main in town
Replace every same age main in the system before returning to that block
Prioritize that block for replacement because local conditions are driving its failures
Lower the zone pressure for the whole system to protect that single block

question: During a break shutdown, valves on both sides of the break are closed yet water still flows into the excavation from a cross street. Which step best finds the remaining feed into the work area?
correctAnswer: Check the cross street valves against the system map and close the open feed

question: A crew isolates a 0.25 m diameter main over a length of 80 m and needs the volume of water the section holds so it can be refilled with treated water. Use 3.1416 for pi and 1,000 L per m³. Round to 0 decimal places. How many litres does the section hold?
explanation: V = (3.1416/4) × d × d × L × 1000. Substitute the stated values: (3.1416/4) × 0.25 × 0.25 × 80 × 1000 = 3927 L. Round only the final result to 0 decimal places.

question: A booster pump delivers 2.7 m³/min into a main with a cross-sectional area of 0.05 m². The operator needs the velocity in metres per second to compare it with the flushing target for that main. Round to 1 decimal place. What is the velocity?
explanation: v = (Q/60) ÷ A. Substitute the stated values: (2.7 ÷ 60) ÷ 0.05 = 0.045 ÷ 0.05 = 0.9 m/s. Round only the final result to 1 decimal place.

question: A tank water surface sits at elevation 412 m and a hydrant at the bottom of the hill sits at elevation 384 m, with the connecting main full and no flow. Use 9.81 kPa per metre of head. Round to 2 decimal places. What is the static pressure at the hydrant?
explanation: P = (surface elevation - hydrant elevation) × 9.81. Substitute the stated values: (412 - 384) × 9.81 = 28 × 9.81 = 274.68 kPa. Round only the final result to 2 decimal places.

question: Two feeds enter a small pressure zone at the same time. One feed supplies 0.75 L/s and the second supplies 45 L/min. The operator needs the combined inflow in litres per second to set a booster pump. Round to 1 decimal place. What is the combined inflow?
explanation: Q total = Q1 + Q2/60. Substitute the stated values: 0.75 + (45 ÷ 60) = 0.75 + 0.75 = 1.5 L/s. Round only the final result to 1 decimal place.

question: Two parallel mains, each 50 m long, are drained for a tie in. One main is 0.20 m in diameter and the other is 0.10 m in diameter. Use 3.1416 for pi. Round to 4 decimal places. How much more water, in m³, does the larger main hold than the smaller main?
explanation: Difference = (3.1416/4) × (d1 × d1 - d2 × d2) × L. Substitute the stated values: 1.5708 - 0.3927 = 1.1781 m³. Round only the final result to 4 decimal places.

question: Water flows at 1.5 m/s through a section of main with a cross-sectional area of 0.08 m², then passes into a narrower section with an area of 0.05 m² carrying the same flow. Round to 1 decimal place. What is the velocity in the narrower section?
explanation: v2 = v1 × A1/A2. Substitute the stated values: the flow is 1.5 × 0.08 = 0.12 m³/s, and 0.12 ÷ 0.05 = 2.4 m/s. Round only the final result to 1 decimal place.

question: A gauge at a low service reads 343.35 kPa. A second service on the same zone sits 12 m higher, and both services are static with no flow. Use 9.81 kPa per metre of head. Round to 2 decimal places. What pressure should the operator expect at the higher service?
explanation: P2 = P1 - (rise × 9.81). Substitute the stated values: 343.35 - (12 × 9.81) = 343.35 - 117.72 = 225.63 kPa. Round only the final result to 2 decimal places.

question: A booster station runs at 25 L/s for 45 minutes during a morning peak and then at 15 L/s for a further 30 minutes. Use 1,000 L per m³. Round to 1 decimal place. What total volume, in m³, did the station deliver?
explanation: V = (Q1 × t1 × 60 + Q2 × t2 × 60)/1000. Substitute the stated values: (67500 + 27000) ÷ 1000 = 94.5 m³. Round only the final result to 1 decimal place.

question: A crew needs a section of 0.50 m diameter main that holds exactly 15.708 m³ when full, so a measured length can be cut before a shutdown. Use 3.1416 for pi. Round to 0 decimal places. What length of main, in metres, holds that volume?
explanation: L = V/((3.1416/4) × d × d). Substitute the stated values: 15.708 ÷ 0.19635 = 80 m. Round only the final result to 0 decimal places.
